full_judgment:
2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule are that opposite party, Rupali Bank, instituted a suit in the aforesaid Artha Rin Adalat against the petitioner for realisation of Bank loan of Taka 4,28,216.50 and obtained a decree. Then the Bank levied the decree in execution in the aforesaid execution Case. On 18.11.99 when the attached property was fixed for auction sale, the executing court ordered for Civil Jail of the Judgment debtor for three months being of the view that he would not be able to satisfy the decreed amount, and issued an warrant of arrest and asked the decree holder to deposit money for the expense for three months. Subsequently on 08.01.2001 the executing court against ordered to issue a warrant of arrest against Judgment debtor for civil prison invoking order 21 Rule 38 of the Code. 

 5. In reply Mr. S.N. Goswami learned Advocate read the Judgment of the Appellate Division in Sultan Jute Mills and submits that Appellate Division has not clearly said anywhere in the judgment that Artha Rin Adalat has specifically barred the Jurisdiction of this Division under section 115 of the Code of respect of an interlocutory order. By reading the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, he also submits that the Ain has not specifically taken away the Jurisdiction of this Division under section 115 of the Code. He submits that it is well established principle, when the Jurisdiction of superior Court like High Court Division is not taken away any law by expressed intention no such ouster can readily be read. He also submits that when the records show before the order is passed for civil provision no notice was issued not any application on behalf of the decree holder was made for sending the Judgment debtor to civil prison in such gross violation of the procedure the executing court passed the order occasioning failure of Justice. This Division at least can exercise the Jurisdiction under Article 109 of the Constitution to ensure fair play. 

 6. We have perused the application and the impugned orders. We have also heard the learned Advocate at length. We have also persued the Judgment of the Sultana Jute Mills and that of House Ara. Begum passed by the Appellate Division. In view of the clear opinion of the Appellate Division in the case of Hosne Ara Begum that revision does not lie against an order of Artha Rin Adalat and that but in a case where a statue bars entertainment of a revision the exercise of supervisory power under Article 109 of the Constitution is not available. We are unable to express our opinion on the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. It is true as admitted by the learned Advocate for the Bank that before order was passed no notice was issued. Even, there was no application made on behalf of the Bank for civil prison of the judgment debtor. It also appears that the view of the executing court that the Judgment debtor could not be able to satisfy the debt under the decree is also not borne out by the record. The law has not permitted to send one to civil prison on such assumption that the Judgment debt will not be able to satisfy the decree. 

 7. Section 51 read with order 21 Rule 37 of the Code says when an application is for execution of a decree for payment of money by arrest and detention in the civil prison of a judgment debtor the executing court is required first to issue a notice calling upon the Judgment debtor to appear before the court on a day fixed to be specified in the notice and show cause as to why he should not be committed to civil prison. We find both the orders were passed without any notice issued against the Judgment debtor rather behind the back of the Judgment debtor. Moreso, payment of money under a decree by arrest and detention in the Civil Prison is one of the modes of execution of a valid decree and that can only be restored to after fulfillment of the conditions as provided under the proviso to section 51 and not otherwise. We are convinced the order for civil prison was passed by the execution court in flagrant violation of the procedure prescribed and such order, no doubt has resulted in serious miscarriage of Justice. But we are undone. In view of the above decisions of the Appellate Division, we find the revision application not maintainable. In view of the decision of the Appellate Division in the Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Vs. Al-haj Md. Shafiuddin Howlader and another 8 BLD (AD) 187, we are unable to invoke even the inherent Jurisdiction to do justice in the case.
